A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same work, renamed from WeatherDiffusion to IntrinsicWeather. v5 includes Supplement A–I; v6 ends after references without that supplement. The judgments below concern content retained or omitted from the supplied PDFs, without assuming that omitted experiments were discontinued.

before.justification: v5 reports original weather-editing, inverse-rendering, downstream perception, ablation and user-study results, including additional experiments in its supplement.

after.justification: v6 retains original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and the 61-participant user study, and reports a qualitative intrinsic-representation ablation finding.

M1.justification: The proposed inverse and forward renderers, IMAA, CLIP-space interpolation and feature distillation remain unchanged. Renaming and clarifying weather-prompt roles do not alter the procedure. The clean-weather-image variant is introduced as an ablation; missing supplementary implementation descriptions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Reported empirical coverage contracts substantially: v5's indoor evaluation on InteriorVerse/Hypersim (Supplement H.1, Table 4), human-focused out-of-distribution examples (supplementary Figure 23), and video-sequence test (main Figure 12) are absent from v6. The main outdoor weather-editing and driving evaluations remain.

E2.justification: TurboEdit, evaluated in v5 Supplement F.1 and supplementary Figure 9, no longer appears in a reported comparison. Comparator membership in the retained main tables and figures is unchanged, including the pixel-space, restoration and rendering baselines.

E3.justification: v6 Section 4.4 introduces a control replacing intrinsic maps with a clean-weather image. The retained experiments use the same reported metrics, ACDC validation set, baseline fine-tuning comparisons and 61-participant, eight-case user study. Missing supplementary settings establish reduced documentation, not revised execution of those experiments.

E4.justification: v6 omits the detailed progressive-training, dataset, interpolation and distillation ablations, cross-weather consistency analysis, out-of-distribution examples and failure cases supplied in v5. The temporal example also disappears. A short intrinsic-representation ablation summary is added, but its detailed evidence is deferred to supplementary material absent from v6.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. The reporting practice remains point estimates and qualitative examples.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 and the 81.67% user-preference summary are identical. v6 omits additional IMAA configurations, indoor scores, separate weather-removal and synthesis preferences of 77.07% and 86.28%, and numerous robustness and failure results. It adds the qualitative finding that clean-weather-image conditioning struggles to preserve scene details; no improved same-setting scores are reported.

T1.justification: Main Equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. However, v5's explicit IMAA pretraining and layer-averaged feature-distillation loss definitions in Supplement C, Equations (4)–(7), are absent from v6. This removes supporting mathematical specification; neither version presents theorem or proof contributions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: intrinsic-space weather editing, IMAA, CLIP-based weather control, two datasets and downstream perception benefits. The reported headline improvements are unchanged. Renaming the framework does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Failure and applicability discussion is substantially reduced. v5 Supplement I explains that occluded backgrounds can be hallucinated and unreliable; this qualification is absent from v6. Section 4.5 also drops video data, computation and resolution constraints while retaining the temporal-consistency warning. v6 adds an interpretation linking the new representation ablation to physical inductive bias.

D1.justification: v6 omits v5's detailed architecture/channel specifications, guidance scales, distillation layers and weights, staged training budgets and hardware, caption/filtering instructions, user-study randomization and downstream checkpoint identifiers. These appeared in Supplement C, D, F.3 and G. Broad dataset-construction information and the dataset-release promise remain, but reproducibility documentation is substantially reduced.

R1.justification: The supplementary review of Retinex and learning-based intrinsic decomposition disappears, together with appendix-only references such as TurboEdit, LoRA and Wonder3D. The bibliography contracts from 63 to 47 entries. Section 2's substantive positioning against the principal rendering and weather-editing approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The document loses the complete supplementary structure, Sections A–I, covering preliminaries, implementation, extended evaluations and failures. Within the retained main paper, editing is limited: framework renaming, author/affiliation updates, an acknowledgement, clearer prompt descriptions, a short added ablation paragraph and shortened limitations.

P2.justification: v6 omits main Figure 12 and the supplement's 25 figures and four tables, substantially reducing the displayed evidence. Retained figures preserve their artwork, with several figures and tables repositioned. Figure 3's caption additionally identifies the displayed predictions as normal maps.

improvement.justification: As supplied, v6 is substantially less reproducible and verifiable: it retains the main claims and scores while omitting detailed training specifications, supporting ablations, broader evaluations and the hallucination limitation, yet continues referring readers to missing supplementary material. Clearer prompt definitions and the brief representation-ablation summary provide limited benefits, but do not offset these losses; the new ablation's detailed evidence is also unavailable.
